version.changelog:
**Improved automation and onboarding for Naver Blog Writer Skill Pack.**

- Added auto token lookup, daemon auto start, and setup/login automation for easier `publish` flow.
- Enhanced error messages with `next_action`, `hint`, and onboarding/billing guidance.
- Updated config to support automatic behaviors (`AUTO_SETUP`, `AUTO_LOGIN_ON_SETUP`, `AUTO_DAEMON_START`, etc).
- Clarified prerequisites for ACP billing and setup, reducing manual steps to a single login.
- Examples and documentation revised for clarity and better user experience.

llm.summary: The SKILL.md describes workflows that require sensitive tokens, local config access, npm package downloads, and optional service installation, but the skill metadata declares no required credentials or install steps — the pieces don't line up.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (publishing to Naver via an ACP offering) is plausible, but the metadata declares no required environment variables or binaries while the SKILL.md requires many (proof/setup tokens, offering execute URL, ACP admin/core API keys, local daemon access). This mismatch between declared requirements and actual instructions is a significant incoherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions instruct the agent to access local daemon endpoints, auto-load ~/.config/naver-thin-runner/config.json if no token is provided, perform onboarding/payment flows, call external offering/control-plane endpoints, and run npm-based runners. These steps read local config and use/require secrets beyond what's declared, and can trigger service installs and login flows — broader scope than the registry metadata indicates.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the registry, but the instructions call 'npx @y80163442/naver-thin-runner', which fetches and runs an npm package at runtime. That implicitly requires Node/npx and performs dynamic code download from the npm registry (third-party package). The lack of an explicit install spec or provenance for that package increases risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md references many sensitive environment values (PROOF_TOKEN, SETUP_ISSUE_URL, SETUP_URL, OPENCLAW_OFFERING_EXECUTE_URL, OPENCLAW_CORE_API_KEY, CONTROL_PLANE_URL, ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY, X_LOCAL_TOKEN) and may auto-read local config containing tokens, yet the registry reports no required env vars. Requesting admin/core API keys and payment/onboarding tokens is proportionate to the feature but must be declared and justified — the omission is concerning.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The setup instructions include installing/running a local daemon and can install services (SETUP_AUTO_SERVICE defaults to 'both'), which introduces persistent system changes. The skill metadata did not call this out; persistent installation plus access to local config and credentials increases the blast radius if misused.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or provide secrets to this skill without additional checks. The SKILL.md expects many secrets and performs dynamic npm downloads and optional service installation, but the registry metadata lists no required envs or install steps — that mismatch is a red flag. Before proceeding: (1) verify the npm package '@y80163442/naver-thin-runner' source and maintainers (review its code and release provenance); (2) require the publisher to explicitly declare all required env vars and binaries and to explain which are strictly needed; (3) avoid supplying ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY / OPENCLAW_CORE_API_KEY or other admin tokens until you confirm trust; (4) if you must test, run in an isolated sandbox or VM and review ~/.config/naver-thin-runner/config.json contents first; (5) confirm billing/onboarding flows (you may be charged) and whether manual human approval is required; (6) prefer an installation path that pins known releases rather than npx on-demand fetch. These steps will reduce risk of credential exposure or unauthorized persistent changes.
